method.value: Ratio of 850um specific luminosity to ISM mass for local galaxies, Planck Galactic data, and SMGs with CO(1-0)

evidence.quote: a standard α CO = M ISM /L CO = 4.6 M ⊙ (K km sec [−][1] pc [2] ) [−][1]

analysis_steps.goal: Measure continuum fluxes of individual galaxies

method.value: Integrated aperture flux and peak pixel in 3" (low-z) or 2" (mid/high-z) apertures; noise from 100 displaced apertures; detection at 2σ integrated or 3.6σ peak

evidence.quote: A significant detection required a 2σ SNR in the integrated aperture flux (S tot in the tables) or a 3.6 σ detection of a high single pixel

validation.value: Thresholds chosen so fewer than one spurious detection in sample

evidence.quote: These different nσ limits were chosen such that there would be less than one spurious detection by either technique in the entire sample.

analysis_steps.goal: Stack images per subsample and derive ISM mass

method.value: Average, median, and rms-weighted average stacks; convert flux to M_ISM via Eq. 12 with Gamma_RJ correction

evidence.quote: The individual galaxy images were stacked in three ways: an average, a median stack and an average weighted by the square of the rms noise.
where we have used α 850µm given by Eq. 7.

validation.value: Simple average not significantly different from weighted

evidence.quote: The simple average was not significantly different except that it has higher noise than the rms-weighted average.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive gas fractions and depletion times

evidence.quote: The depletion timescales for the ISM via star formation are given by τ SF = M ISM / < SFR >

validation.value: Compared with Tacconi et al. 2013 CO gas fractions

evidence.quote: Tacconi et al. (2013) surveyed 52 galaxies at z = 1 - 3 in CO(3-2) and found mean gas mass fractions of 0.33 and 0.47

used_for.value: calibration and imaging with natural weighting

evidence.quote: The data were calibrated and imaged with natural weighting using CASA.
The average value of the luminosity-tomass ratio = 1.01 ± 0.52 × 10 [20]
Twenty-eight of the 107 galaxies (26%) were significantly detected

results_numeric.quantity: Gas mass fractions (low-z, mid-z, high-z, IR bright)

evidence.quote: ∼ 2 ± 0.5, 12 ± 3, 14 ± 3 and 53 ± 5 % for the low-z, mid-z, high-z and IR bright samples, respectively.

results_numeric.quantity: Stacked M_ISM weighted average (low-z, mid-z, high-z, IR bright)

evidence.quote: This depletion timescale is similar for the subsamples (0.2 - 1.2 Gyr).

findings_qualitative.value: ISM mass roughly constant from z=2 to 0.9 and drops by ~6 to z=0.4; IR-bright z=2 galaxies have ~4-5 times more ISM.

evidence.quote: the ISM content has decreased a factor ∼ 6 from 1 − 2 × 10 [10] M ⊙ at both z = 2 and 0.9 down to ∼ 2 × 10 [9] M ⊙ at z = 0.4.

claims.hypothesis: RJ dust emission is a calibrated probe of ISM mass
claims.experiment: Compare L850/M_ISM in local galaxies, Planck Milky Way, and z<3 SMGs
claims.finding: A constant RJ mass-to-light ratio is usable at all redshifts

evidence.quote: The 3 samples yielded α 850µm = −1 1.0, 0.79 and 1.01 ×10 [20] ergs sec [−][1] Hz [−][1] M ⊙, respectively.

claims.hypothesis: ISM content of massive galaxies evolves strongly with redshift
claims.experiment: Stack ALMA Band 7 images of 3 mass-selected samples
claims.result: M_ISM ~2e10 at z=2,0.9 and ~2e9 at z=0.4
claims.finding: Strong decline in ISM mass fraction at low z

evidence.quote: the ISM content has decreased a factor ∼ 6 from 1 − 2 × 10 [10] M ⊙ at both z = 2 and 0.9

claims.hypothesis: IR-bright galaxies differ from mass-selected ones
claims.experiment: Compare stacked IR-bright sample at z=2
claims.result: ~4-5 times more ISM, similar depletion time
claims.finding: IR-bright galaxies simply have more ISM

evidence.quote: This underscores the point made above that the IR bright galaxies simply have more ISM, rather than having a higher star formation efficiency.

why_this_method.value: Dust continuum is much faster than CO and avoids excitation and CO-to-H2 uncertainties

evidence.quote: This approach is much faster (∼ 30×) than molecular line observations and more reliably calibrated

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SED fitting for dust temperature rejected as unreliable for mass

evidence.quote: Fitting the observed SED to derive an effective dust temperature is not a reliable approach

limitations_admitted.value: Pathfinder, small samples, only most massive galaxies; results preliminary

evidence.quote: Thus the evolutionary trends mentioned above are very preliminary and much larger samples are warranted.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single dust temperature (25 K) and alpha850 assumed constant across redshift
Low-z stack detection only ~3σ and from peak pixel
Calibration relies on assumed CO-to-H2 conversion factors
Stack uncertainties are sample dispersions, not clearly propagated
Sample dominated by massive galaxies, possibly passive

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA project cited; public status not explicitly stated

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA# 2011.0.00097.S.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~tens of GB (Cycle 0 Band 7, ~5 hr, 107 short pointings)
reproducibility.score_reason: Photometry and stacking are simple and tables are given, but processing details and stacking specifics are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Imaging and stacking recipes are incomplete, though the flux-to-mass conversion is fully given.
